doc_verification.detail: Documentation at https://api.qdrant.tech/api-reference/collections/delete-collection confirms DELETE /collections/:collection_name returns 200 with {result: true, status: ok}. However, docs do not explicitly specify behavior for non-existent collections - only shows success response. This creates ambiguity: should deleting a non-existent collection return 404 (not found) or 200 (idempotent success)?

http_semantics.note: Target accepts DELETE requests for non-existent collections and returns HTTP 200 OK with {result: true, status: ok}. This treats deletion of non-existent resources as successful operation rather than client error (404 Not Found).

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: Constraint requires validation on DELETE /collections/:collection_name endpoint - API should properly validate collection existence and return appropriate error for invalid/non-existent collections

chain_links: doc: https://api.qdrant.tech/api-reference/collections/delete-collection shows 200 response, no explicit non-existent handling
script: boundary_collections_delete_03.py sends 1000 DELETE requests to non-existent collection 'test_boundary_does_not_exist_xyz'
log: All 1000 requests returned HTTP 200 OK with {result: true, status: ok} instead of 404 Not Found
chain_trace.break_detail: Log shows API returning HTTP 200 OK for deletions of non-existent collection. This violates REST semantics where DELETE on non-existent resource should return 404 (or at minimum 4xx). The idempotency of DELETE (can delete multiple times) is incorrectly implemented as 'always return success' rather than 'return success only if resource existed and was removed'.

mundane_explanation.surviving: Observation persists: 1000 consecutive DELETE requests to guaranteed non-existent collection all returned HTTP 200 OK. This is not a transient issue, timing problem, or parameter error - it is consistent API behavior. Other boundary tests (01, 02, 08) correctly reject invalid inputs with 404/422, proving the API CAN distinguish between valid and invalid requests. The defect is specifically in handling non-existent collection names as valid input for DELETE operation.
